idea.value: Prospecting is a search that never stops counting: a list doubles from 1 to over half a million matches in 7.3 s until the picture breaks, then the product turns one described opportunity into a single person with a full-match badge.

audience.value: B2B sellers and founders who do outbound prospecting and already know lead databases: the copy speaks in job titles, company revenue bands, headcount bands, installed software and contact counts, never explains what a lead is.
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 0.27-4.5 (query naming a role, a company type and a revenue floor)
speech-text.json screenText 6.53-14 (role-at-company-type label over the montage)
speech-text.json screenText 24.6-36.5 (headcount band, software used, contact counts)

value.device: Cursor-anchored typewriter: a long, very specific query types itself into a field while the camera tracks the caret (text runs off the left edge), then the field shrinks to a strip above a person who sits waiting; a hard cut to black asks the question on its own line.
value.description: 0-1.93 s: query types at about 2 frames a character, framed so tight that only the last 25-35 characters show (OCR box x = 0). 1.93 s: a one-frame block glitch (F115) and a cut to a wide, near-white studio with one seated person under the query strip (13% from the top). 4.73 s: hard cut to black, 7 frames of nothing (F284-F291), then a line types on black, the newest word in accent red for 6-7 frames. 5.50 s: a 4-frame polarity flash and the line jumps to about 1.7x. The viewer is given the problem as an act (searching) before any product is named; the name arrives 20 s later.

value.purpose: Set the task: a hyper-specific search
value.retentionDevice: Text growing at the caret, camera chasing it
value.content: A query types itself in a white field, framed tight on the caret.

value.purpose: Put a human under the query: the person the search is for
value.retentionDevice: Stillness after speed; the query becomes a small strip at the top
value.content: Wide near-white studio, one person seated at a white desk, centred; the query as a pill at 13% from the top.

value.purpose: Name the act as a question
value.retentionDevice: Black after white; a single line typing; red on the newest word
value.content: On black, a short line types and punches in to about 1.7x through a polarity flash.

value.purpose: Show the problem as overload: every result is a person, and the count doubles until it is meaningless
value.retentionDevice: Accelerating cuts (1.53 s down to 2 frames) synced to a doubling odometer counter; flash frames on swaps
value.content: Fixed layout: query strip top, count left of a seated person, a found-label and a name card right. Twenty subjects in 7.3 s, count 1 to 524 288.

value.purpose: The turn: state the requirement, then break it, then reset
value.retentionDevice: Kinetic word on black, letter-by-letter case flip, corruption, then black and silence
value.content: A two-word line types, swaps to a one-word adjective through a glitch, the word flips to capitals letter by letter, corrupts into symbols and smears to black; 0.57 s of black.

value.retentionDevice: 3D mark pulled out of an extreme close-up, then a pixel ring blooming on white
value.content: A glossy red extruded mark glitches in full-frame and pulls back to a speck on black; hard cut to white where a pixel-mosaic ring grows from the mark and the wordmark types on beside it over a warm peach gradient.

value.purpose: Proof: the search done in the product, in plain language
value.retentionDevice: Caret-tracking close-ups alternating with wides; result count falling with each added clause
value.content: The real interface: a natural-language query is typed and extended clause by clause (bracketed placeholders highlighted in coral); after the first clause the count races up to about 12 500 under a dot-matrix result visual, then falls to about 2 300 as each later clause is added.

value.purpose: Submit and narrow to a short list; restate the promise as an instruction
value.retentionDevice: A colour wash after the press, a count ticking down
value.content: Pointer presses the submit control; a pink wash floods the frame, a ring ripples from the pointer, and a small result count resolves and ticks from about 211 down to 132; then a one-line instruction drifts across.

value.purpose: Payoff: one exact person instead of half a million
value.retentionDevice: Line completes on white, camera tilts down from it to a person; a thumbs-up and a counting match badge
value.content: Hard cut to white, the second half of the line types; the camera tilts down from the line to a seated person; a hand enters with a thumbs-up and a green badge counts to a full match above him; he stands and walks out right.

value.retentionDevice: The whole plate defocuses; mark and name type on over it
value.content: Over the defocused studio the mark appears, the wordmark types on at about 3 frames a letter, then a black pill with a one-line demo offer sits under it until the end.

payoff.value: A single seated person with a thumbs-up and a badge counting up to a full match (44.2-44.5 s), set against the 524 288 faces of the montage: the product's value is told as subtraction, from a flood to one.

callToAction.value: Wordmark centred with a black pill beneath offering a free demo at the product's address, held 5.9 s (50.4-56.53) with no motion after the type-on; the final frame is the card itself, no fade.

whyItWorks: The problem is shown as a number the viewer can feel: a counter that doubles on every cut while cuts shrink from 1.53 s to 2 frames, so overload is experienced as speed before it is read.
Every search result is a human face in the same seat and framing, so the fixed layout makes each swap readable at 2-6 frames: only the face, the number and the name card change.
The film resets twice with black: 7 frames of black before the question (4.73 s) and 0.57 s of black with near-silence before the brand (16.93-17.5 s), so the reveal lands on a clean slate.
Typing is the through-line: the hook, the question, the requirement, the demo and the logo all arrive by caret, so the product's input (one typed description) is the film's grammar.
The payoff inverts the montage: same studio, same kind of person, but one, still, and approved, which makes the claim of precision without stating it.
